title: Certificate in AI Agents for Business Operations
summary: Implement AI agents in business processes such as customer service triage, procurement, operations, and workflow coordination.
capstone: Business-process agent with an ROI case and governance plan.
delivery: Self-paced draft modules with proposed weekend workshops, peer discussion and office hours; no cohort scheduled.
outcomes: O1: Map decision boundaries and evidence requirements for a procurement intake process.
O2: Construct and explain a bounded prototype for a procurement intake process.
O3: Evaluate ordinary, ambiguous and adversarial cases against a baseline.
O4: Demonstrate privacy minimization, human approval and recoverable failure.
O5: Defend a operations improvement portfolio with reproducible evidence and limitations.

modules.title: Define the decision boundary
modules.lesson: An assistant can suggest an action without permission to perform it. Name the decision owner, allowed inputs, prohibited outputs and measurable baseline before selecting a model.

activity.title: Define the decision boundary — applied workshop
activity.objective: O1: Map decision boundaries and evidence requirements for a procurement intake process.
activity.overview: You support a procurement intake process. Draw an input-to-review map with two mandatory human checkpoints.

steps.title: Concept setup · 10 minutes
steps.text: An assistant can suggest an action without permission to perform it. Name the decision owner, allowed inputs, prohibited outputs and measurable baseline before selecting a model.

steps.title: Implementation · 20 minutes
steps.text: Map each ID to review if confidence is missing or below 0.8, otherwise ready_for_review. Neither route executes an action. Open the starter notebook or visual workflow simulator.

steps.title: Task · 20 minutes
steps.text: Draw an input-to-review map with two mandatory human checkpoints. Record a normal, missing-input and human-review case.

steps.title: Research and discussion · 15 minutes
steps.text: Compare with a peer, cite your reading and identify a failure condition.

steps.title: Wrap-up · 5 minutes
steps.text: Explain why a simulation is not a production-ready system; name the accountable owner.

reflection: What evidence changes your decision?
Which error is more costly here?
What information can you avoid retaining?
activity.submission: Draft cohort policy: 2–3-page APA-style paper with relevant code, output screenshots and citations. Word/PDF upload and Sunday 11:59 PM deadline need a scheduled cohort; no live deadline is set.
activity.integrity: AI coaching on concepts and ungraded practice is allowed with disclosure. Graded reasoning must be your own.

modules.labTask: Map each ID to review if confidence is missing or below 0.8, otherwise ready_for_review. Neither route executes an action.

miniLabs.title: Missing-input stress test
miniLabs.task: Replace every fourth confidence with None. Re-run and explain the changed results.

miniLabs.title: Scale and subgroup check
miniLabs.task: Use the 60-row assignment dataset; compare queues and state a sampling limitation.

quiz.prompt: Which boundary is testable?
choices: A named task with allowed actions and a human escalation owner
A promise to automate the department
Skip review and trust the output.
quiz.explanation: An assistant can suggest an action without permission to perform it. Name the decision owner, allowed inputs, prohibited outputs and measurable baseline before selecting a model.

quiz.prompt: Your team supporting a procurement intake process cannot reproduce a result. What next?
choices: Publish because the report looks complete.
Reproduce the inputs, versions and checks before accepting the claim.
Remove failing examples.
quiz.explanation: Keep failures visible. A claim needs reproducible evidence.

quiz.prompt: Which artifact best demonstrates define the decision boundary?
choices: Draw an input-to-review map with two mandatory human checkpoints. Include results and limitations.
A screenshot with no inputs or explanation.
An assertion of perfect accuracy.
quiz.explanation: A concrete artifact and observed evidence support review.

modules.liveSession: Compare two approaches to define the decision boundary and defend the review boundary.
modules.announcement: Module 1: Define the decision boundary. Review the objective, run practice cases and bring a failure to discussion. Cohort dates pending.

masteryPath.remediation: Re-read the concept, repeat the missing-input task and explain the mistake before retrying.

capstonePackage.exemplar: A fictional approval queue retains missing scores, routes uncertainty to review and never executes updates. Its evidence pack records input versions, thresholds, subgroup counts, failed cases and a rollback owner. Adapt this scaffold to the program brief. This is not a finished capstone solution.

transferPolicy: No automatic credit. Map outcomes and assessed evidence; an educator approves equivalence and prevents duplicate credit. Dependencies #1–#14 remain TBC.
